headline: In 1908 something exploded over Siberia and flattened 80 million trees.
slides: At about 7:17am, people near the Tunguska river saw a fireball cross the sky.
It flattened around 80 million trees across 2,150 square km of forest.
Whatever it was blew up 5 to 10 km above the ground. Nothing hit the surface.
Nobody reached the site until a Soviet expedition 19 years later. The trees lay pointing outward like spokes.
Alien spacecraft, a mini black hole, antimatter. All suggested at some point.
Scientists now agree it was a small asteroid or comet exploding in the air. The largest impact in recorded history.
sources: Sources: NASA, EarthSky, CBC, Russian Academy of Sciences expedition records (1927)
